title: A paragraph holding only a VML horizontal rule (v:rect o:hr, hrstd or not) is one line of the rule run's own face and size plus the paragraph spacing, whatever marks wrap the run; a rule taller than that line grows it
source: probe build.py -> Word for Mac direct PDF (2026-11-02), pymupdf control baselines (Calibri 11 pitch 13.44) and the rule's filled rect: Georgia 14 bold run at line 276 -> 18.24 pt paragraph (= 14 x 1.136 x 1.15), the title-page triple rule / Georgia 14 text / rule spans 54.96 between the controls (3 near-equal lines), an inherited Calibri 11 run 13.41 (the mark's Georgia 14 does not size it: 13.41 again), Georgia 14 bold at line 240 15.81, a 6 pt rule under Calibri 11 still 13.41, a 20 pt rule 24.93 (= 19.6 drawn + 2.36 above + the 2.96 descent below), after 160 / line 259 22.53. The stroke is drawn 0.4 pt thinner than declared and its bottom sits one descent above the baseline. gen before the fix: a bold rule run (strong wrapper) measured two lines (39.5 pt) because the trailing-break phantom escaped the span-only selector, and the rule line used the document's Calibri factor instead of Georgia's (19.6 vs 18.24)

cases.note: bold Georgia 14 rule run alone at line 276: one Georgia line, not two
control to control across rule / Georgia 14 text / rule
6 pt rule under Calibri 11: the font line still decides
20 pt rule: Word adds 2.36 above and the descent below (gen 22.95: rule + descent only)
o:hr without o:hrstd: the same line
run without rPr under a Georgia 14 mark: the run's inherited face sizes the line, not the mark
